title: Cylindrical thin strip thickness and Poisson sensitivity
source: A Kirchhoff cylindrical-bending strip: the two long edges y=0 and y=1 impose u_y=0 and rotation about x=0, so the width strain and curvature vanish and D=E t^3/[12(1-nu^2)] applies. The reference ratios are the closed-form logarithmic derivatives; the tolerance is the two-mesh difference plus the closed-form Timoshenko shear/rotary correction.

quantities.quantity: t times tip deflection derivative divided by deflection
quantities.reason: Kirchhoff cylindrical bending gives w proportional to t^-3. The Timoshenko estimate uses w=P[L^3/(3EI)+L/(kappa G A)] with r=3EI/(kappa G A L^2)=1.95e-5; its relative correction is 1.30e-5, and the 4x1 versus 8x1 mesh difference is 8.47e-6, so 1e-4 covers their sum.

quantities.quantity: t times first frequency derivative divided by frequency
quantities.reason: Kirchhoff bending with shell mass proportional to t gives f proportional to t. For beta_1=1.875104, the Timoshenko estimate has eta_s=2.2854e-5 and eta_r=7.3250e-6, giving a 3.02e-5 correction; the two-mesh difference is 2.16e-7.

quantities.quantity: nu times tip deflection derivative divided by deflection
quantities.reason: Kirchhoff gives -2 nu^2/(1-nu^2). With the same Timoshenko expression and G=E/[2(1+nu)], the shear correction is 4.22e-5 relative; the two-mesh difference is 2.76e-5, so 1e-4 is a bounded sum.

quantities.quantity: nu times first frequency derivative divided by frequency
quantities.reason: Kirchhoff frequency theory gives nu^2/(1-nu^2). The first-mode Timoshenko correction uses R_nu - 0.5 eta_s nu/(1-nu)/(1+eta_s+eta_r), a 4.95e-5 relative correction; the two-mesh difference is 1.24e-7.
